findings.claim: COMMIT TO /STAGE tells the artist it is routing through the consent gate and does nothing of the kind - no GateProposal, no /stage write, no queue entry. It only sets a UI substate.

Gate Approve and Gate Reject are optimistic UI over a swallowed exception - mark_decided and decision_announced fire unconditionally even when HumanGate is absent or decide() raises. A rejection that never landed still reads as rejected. This is consent theatre.

The 21 slash commands do not invoke their implementations - the palette entry's send string is the description text, so /diagnose sends prose to the LLM and scene_doctor.py never runs. ~7,500 LOC of feature modules are bypassed this way.
Emergency halt has no surface in the shipped panel. HALT exists only in the unreachable chat_panel tree, so CLAUDE.md Safety Rule 11 ('emergency halt is immediate') has no artist-reachable trigger.
The panel has two entrypoints and only one ships. 24 of 71 modules are unreachable from the shipped entrypoint, including ~10,500 LOC of implemented feature modules with zero callers.

Two tests pin dead or no-op behaviour as green: tests/test_panel_faces.py:168 asserts only face state for the ACCEPT no-op, and tests/test_v5_features.py:54 is an import-smoke test artificially keeping the dead ui/ package alive.
The panel does NOT need the WS bridge - it dispatches in-process via ToolExecutor -> SynapseHandler. The down bridge (L1.F1) does not gate panel capability. Load-bearing for L4.

The accent token has a THIRD source outside the repository: ~/.synapse/design/tokens.py:21 = #00D4FF, injected onto sys.path by tokens.py:15 and re-exported. The panel's accent is machine-dependent - an in-repo token change can be silently overridden per-workstation.

L4's stated token oracle is uncheckable as worded. styles.py is 822 LOC (not 705) and defines ZERO tokens - it is a stylesheet factory of 41 get_*_stylesheet() functions. The checkable form is the 36 token names it REFERENCES, recorded in the inventory artifact.

Two of five G3 slices have NO baseline: the hython-offscreen invocation was permission-denied four times (denied, not failed). The live offscreen build and the v9 invariants - the two most L4-relevant slices - are ungraded.

The relay's premise that a muted green must be ADDED is wrong - OK_SOFT #6FBF8E already exists and is live in 4 files. Adding a second green would recreate the 3-source token gremlin inside the status family.

Two raw-hex accent leaks bypass the token system in the shipped tree: message_formatter.py:39 hardcodes #8FB3D9 (right value, unlinked) and render_preflight.py:927 hardcodes #00D4FF inside an HTML string.

The relay's providers/ figure is wrong by an order of magnitude - it is 1,506 LOC, not 136, and all five engines are implemented. The real deficiency is that only one (claude) is usable without configuration.

Three of the relay's L4 design premises do not survive measurement: the 0.5px hairline does not exist (HAIR is 1px), no network-peek component exists at all, and the title tracking is 2.24px not 2.5px.

for_ruling.question: Three panel affordances lie to the artist about safety-critical operations: COMMIT-to-/stage claims consent-gate routing that never happens, and gate Approve/Reject report decisions that may never have reached HumanGate. Who lands the fix, and when?
options: Fix now as a hotfix before any restyle - a lying consent surface is the worst class of defect in this repo
Fold into the L2.R3 family-wide 'does a failure owe the caller truth' contract and fix together
Defer to post-T.1
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1 for the two gate paths, option 2 for COMMIT. The gate widget is three lines of unconditional emit that should be conditional; that is a small, safe, high-value fix. COMMIT is a larger missing-implementation and belongs with the L2 doctrine ruling.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Highest in the relay. SYNAPSE's differentiator is receipts and reversibility; a consent surface that reports decisions it did not make attacks that differentiator directly.

for_ruling.question: Emergency halt has no artist-reachable surface in the shipped panel - it exists only in the dead chat_panel tree. CLAUDE.md Safety Rule 11 says halt is immediate.
options: Restore HALT to synapse_panel.py
Accept LLM-mediated halt as sufficient
Add halt to the Ctrl+K palette only
for_ruling.recommendation: Restore it as a persistent affordance, not a palette entry. A stop button you have to search for is not a stop button. This is the one ORPHAN worth reviving on safety grounds alone, and reviving a single safety control is not a T.4 product-identity decision.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High. It is a stated safety rule with no implementation on the shipped surface.

for_ruling.question: The 21 slash commands send description prose to the LLM instead of dispatching, bypassing ~7,500 LOC of implemented feature modules (scene_doctor, apex_trace, explain_mode and 18 more).
options: Wire the palette entries to real dispatch
Remove the slash commands from the palette until they dispatch
Leave
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 2 now, option 1 later. Removing them is honest and cheap; wiring 21 entries is real work. A menu entry that silently does something other than its name is exactly what L4's scope fence calls 'how a panel lies'.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Medium-high. Every use is a silent capability failure the artist reads as an LLM shortcoming.

for_ruling.question: L4's token oracle is uncheckable as written (styles.py defines zero tokens). Restate it?
options: Restate as: the 162 tokens in the inventory artifact, plus the 36 names styles.py references, must all survive
Drop the oracle
Keep the literal wording
for_ruling.recommendation: Restate. The artifact harness/notes/panel_token_inventory_before.json exists precisely so this becomes assertable rather than eyeballed.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Blocks L4's acceptance criteria from being machine-checkable.

for_ruling.question: The accent token's third source is ~/.synapse/design/tokens.py - OUTSIDE the repo, injected onto sys.path by tokens.py:15. It makes the panel accent machine-dependent. Does L4 get authority to sever that re-export?
options: Sever the sys.path re-export - in-repo tokens become authoritative
Keep it as a user-override feature and document it
Leave, and extend the _ds.SIGNAL pattern to the 6 cyan sites instead
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 3 for L4 (additive, safe, does not break test_hda_panel), then option 1 as a separate decision. Severing an out-of-repo sys.path injection is not chrome work and should not ride inside a restyle commit.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Medium. Today a token fix can be silently overridden on any workstation with that directory.

for_ruling.question: Two of five G3 slices have no baseline because the hython-offscreen invocation was permission-denied. L4 would ship ungraded on live-build and v9-invariant checks.
options: Grant the hython-offscreen invocation and re-baseline before L4 lands
Let L4 ship on the 3 gradeable slices and note the gap
Block L4
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1. It is a permission grant, not engineering work, and panel verification is hython-offscreen-only by standing convention - the other two slices are exactly the ones that catch interactive-target and same-pane-law regressions.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Direct: L4 lands unverifiable on 40% of its own gate.

for_ruling.question: The relay states providers/ is 136 LOC against a five-engine claim, and pre-seeds R4 as 'fix the claim now, the code after T.1'. Measurement refutes the premise - it is 1,506 LOC with all five implemented.
options: Restate the public claim as 'five engines, one configured out of the box'
Leave the claim as-is - it is technically accurate
Reduce the claim to one engine
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1. The code is not the problem; the out-of-box experience is. 'Five swappable engines' is true and misleading at the same time, and the honest sentence is one line longer.
